headline: Single team-controlled EOA guardian holds immediate unilateral control over pDAO settings and critical protocol parameters with no timelock or multi-sig requirement.
short_headline: EOA guardian, no timelock, T1 path

findings.text: RocketStorage guardian at 0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e (pinned address_book role confirmed) is an EOA controlled by Rocket Pool Pty Ltd / team; getGuardian() on RocketStorage (0x1d8f8f00cfa6758d7bE78336684788Fb0ee0Fa46) returns exactly this address at block 25086022.

Core contracts (RocketStorage, RocketTokenRETH at 0xae78736cd615f374d3085123a210448e74fc6393) are immutable / non-proxy (verified exact match on Etherscan, no implementation/admin slots); protocol upgrade surface is via pDAO settings updates to RocketStorage key-value registry and contract addresses; mixed upgradeability with guardian-controlled pDAO pathway reaching core logic.

Fast-path execution for pDAO settings / parameter changes / treasury spends / feature disables is immediate single-transaction by guardian EOA (no MIN_DELAY, no timelock contract, no queue/execute stages); oDAO pathway uses majority vote with post-proposal delay only (no execution timelock); no uncontested multi-stage path with measurable delay found.

Reachable multisigs: GMC (9 members per RPIP-26, multisig per RPIP-10 requiring ≥3/5 or higher threshold, powers limited to grants/incentives distribution and member rotation); IMC (similar structure for rETH/RPL liquidity incentives); Security Council proposed (RPIP-33 / 2024 forum) but not yet displacing guardian EOA on core pDAO settings path; guardian EOA holds primary upgrade / settings / emergency powers.

pDAO uses on-chain elements (RocketDAOProtocolVerifier at 0xd1f7e573cdC64FC0B201ca37aB50bC7Dd880040A for proposal verification / challenges) + Snapshot off-chain voting; proposal threshold / votingPeriod / quorum not readable on-chain in this run (bootstrapping phase); guardian EOA currently bypasses full token-weighted governance for settings changes.

Guardian EOA provides emergency powers: immediate disable of protocol features / modify pDAO settings / set RPL inflation shares / set minipool penalty rates / spend pDAO-allocated RPL (no separate time-capped emergency multisig or governance vote required; powers active as of latest on-chain read).

Highest tier on uncontested fast path is T1: guardian EOA can alter economic parameters (collateral.target, deposit.pool.maximum, penalty rates per RPIP-16/ forum), redirect protocol revenue shares, spend treasury RPL, and disable core features affecting user fund flows / exits / staking mechanics (named functions/settings in RocketStorage / pDAO pathway); no on-chain bound preventing T1 blast radius.

steelman.red: Single EOA guardian (0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e) controls pDAO settings pathway with zero delay or multi-party approval, enabling immediate T1 actions on protocol parameters and treasury that reach user funds and core staking mechanics.
steelman.orange: pDAO / oDAO provide on-chain governance elements and multisig committees (GMC/IMC) for some operational scopes, with plans for Security Council transition; many actions require votes even if guardian currently shortcuts settings.
steelman.green: Protocol has public RPIPs, DAO forum, and on-chain verifier contracts moving toward token-weighted pDAO governance with diversified node operator participation; guardian powers are transitional and documented for handover.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because the highest reachable tier on the uncontested fast path is T1 (guardian EOA can unilaterally alter critical economic / penalty / feature settings with no timelock or multi-sig), as directly evidenced by getGuardian() read, Etherscan verification of RocketStorage, and dao.rocketpool.net forum documentation of guardian powers (no delay, immediate execution).

evidence.shows: getGuardian() returns exactly 0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e at block 25086022; confirms current RocketStorage guardian EOA.
RocketStorage verified exact match (v0.7.6); exposes getGuardian / setGuardian / setAddress / setUint and storage key-value functions; no proxy pattern; central registry for all protocol contracts.

Guardian EOA (Rocket Pool Pty Ltd controlled) holds immediate power over pDAO settings pathway, RPL inflation, penalty rates, treasury spends with no timelock or delay; GMC (9 members), IMC multisigs detailed with RPIP-10/26 thresholds; pDAO settings currently guardian-controlled (bootstrapping); no execution timelock for pDAO/oDAO pathways.
Team/guardian currently controls pDAO guardian role; Security Council formation proposed to replace immediate team control over feature disables.
RocketTokenRETH (rETH) verified, immutable (no proxy/admin), constructor references RocketStorage; no separate owner/guardian function.
Public canonical source repo for all core contracts (RocketStorage.sol, DAO contracts, settings, etc.); updated 2026.

unknowns: C3: exact numeric values for any oDAO proposal delay or pDAO votingPeriod/quorum (not readable via simple view calls in this run; bootstrapping phase may bypass)
C4: current exact signer list / threshold / non-insider % for active Security Council multisig (proposed in 2024 RPIP-33/forum but status post-Saturn unclear; only GMC/IMC details confirmed)
C5: whether full RPL-token-weighted on-chain governance (with timelock) has fully replaced guardian shortcut for all T1/T2 actions as of analysis_date

protocol_metadata.about: Rocket Pool is a decentralized liquid staking protocol on Ethereum. Users deposit ETH to mint rETH (a liquid staking receipt token that earns staking rewards). Node operators run Ethereum validators with only 8 ETH + RPL collateral (instead of 32 ETH) and earn commissions. Governance is via pDAO (RPL-weighted, currently in bootstrapping with team EOA guardian shortcut) and oDAO for oracle reporting; RPL also provides insurance backing.

headline: Permissionless on-chain rETH redeem / minipool exit functions exist and are frontend-independent, but redemption is subject to liquidity/queue mechanics that guardian EOA can influence indefinitely via settings; no guaranteed forced-exit escape hatch today.

findings.text: User-facing exit functions: RocketTokenRETH burn/redeem (rETH → ETH when deposit pool has excess balance); node operator minipool exit / withdrawal address claims / penalty claims; RocketDepositPool excess balance withdrawals; pending withdrawal address confirmations in RocketStorage.

Burn/redeem and minipool exit functions are permissionless (no onlyRole / onlyWhitelisted on core paths); request placement unconditional; claim/finalized settlement depends on available ETH liquidity in deposit pool or validator exits (no admin signature required for placement or claim when liquidity exists).

Pause / disable guards exist via guardian-modifiable settings (network.reth.collateral.target, deposit.pool.maximum per RPIP-16/forum); guardian EOA can immediately disable features / alter liquidity parameters with no time cap (setGuardian / setUint on RocketStorage); no explicit PAUSE_INFINITELY role found but equivalent via settings; oDAO majority vote provides slower governance path.

Emergency path: guardian EOA immediate feature disable (unilateral, indefinite until reversed); governance path via pDAO (currently same EOA shortcut) or oDAO majority; no separate time-capped emergency multisig distinct from guardian.

Queued redemption exists (withdrawal queue proposals in RPIP-71 / Saturn 2; current liquidity via deposit pool excess + node operator exits); max queue duration / daily caps not pinned on-chain in this run; guardian settings (collateral.target=0) can prioritize / starve queue fulfillment per forum RPIPs.

No permissionless forced-exit / escape-hatch for rETH holders today (RPIP-71 for EIP-7002 forced validator exits proposed for Saturn 2, not yet live); users can exit via secondary market (DEX) or wait for protocol liquidity / node operator voluntary exits; no admin-gated escape for adversarial scenarios.
All exit functions directly callable on-chain via Etherscan Write Contract tab, generic wallets, or SDK (no frontend required; rETH is standard ERC-20 with public burn/mint when conditions met).

steelman.red: Guardian EOA can unilaterally alter liquidity parameters and disable features indefinitely with no time cap or multi-sig, effectively gating or starving rETH redemption claims; no full forced-exit escape hatch exists today.
steelman.orange: Core exit functions (rETH burn when liquidity available, minipool withdrawals) are permissionless and on-chain; guardian influence is limited to economic parameters rather than direct pause on finalized claims; secondary market always provides an exit path.
steelman.green: No contract-level whitelist or admin signature required for any exit function; rETH is widely liquid on DEXes; node operators permissionlessly exit their minipools; on-chain redeem exists and is frontend-independent.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because exit functions are permissionless and directly on-chain (E7, E2), but redemption/claim finalization depends on liquidity queues that the guardian EOA can influence indefinitely via settings changes (E3/E5) without a hard time cap or separate emergency multisig, and no permissionless forced-exit exists yet (E6); this matches orange criteria for broad-scope pausability via governance/guardian path.

evidence.shows: Guardian EOA confirmed active; controls settings that affect deposit pool / collateral / liquidity (per RPIP/forum cross-reference).
RocketTokenRETH verified; public burn / redeem / transfer functions (standard ERC-20 mechanics gated only by protocol liquidity logic in storage).
Guardian can modify pDAO settings including collateral.target and deposit.pool.maximum (directly impacts redemption liquidity); immediate power with no delay.
Current rETH withdrawal relies on deposit pool liquidity and node operator exits; forced-exit mechanism (EIP-7002) proposed for future Saturn 2, not live.

unknowns: E3: exact implementation of any whenNotPaused or disable flag on rETH redeem / claim paths (settings-based equivalent confirmed via guardian powers but no direct hasRole/paused() read in this run)
E5: documented maximum queue duration or daily withdrawal cap for rETH redemption (RPIP-71 discusses but no on-chain constant pinned)
E6: whether any on-chain escape-hatch contract or permissionless forced validator exit function is already deployed post-Saturn

protocol_metadata.about: Rocket Pool is a decentralized liquid staking protocol on Ethereum. Users deposit ETH to mint rETH (a liquid staking receipt token that earns staking rewards). Node operators run Ethereum validators with only 8 ETH + RPL collateral (instead of 32 ETH) and earn commissions. Governance is via pDAO (RPL-weighted, currently in bootstrapping with team EOA guardian shortcut) and oDAO for oracle reporting; RPL also provides insurance backing.

headline: No external dependency can cause loss of user principal; oDAO reporting and Ethereum beacon chain are the only material touchpoints, both with strong mitigations and no governance-mutable hot-swap of untrusted externals without exit window.

findings.text: Core contracts call/register via RocketStorage only; no external price oracle (rETH/ETH rate derived from oDAO validator balance reports + beacon chain data); no AMM / lending pool / bridge calls in core staking path.

oDAO (Oracle DAO) reports validator balances and rETH exchange rate; diversified node operator set with staking / slashing incentives; mis-reporting affects rate/ yield visibility but not principal (ETH remains staked on beacon chain); majority vote required for oDAO actions.
No bridge or cross-chain messaging dependency for core TVL or user flows (all on Ethereum L1; rETH bridges exist but optional and not required for staking/exit).
No nested collateral / restaking chain; direct ETH staking into beacon chain validators via permissionless node operators; no LRT / receipt-of-receipt propagation risk.
No fork lineage (DeFiLlama forkedFrom empty for Rocket Pool).

Fallbacks: rate sanity bounds / rebase limits in rETH contract (enforced on-chain); oDAO challenges / verification via RocketDAOProtocolVerifier; withdrawal queues absorb temporary liquidity shortfalls; all documented as LIVE and enforcing.
No sequencer / L2 dependency (native Ethereum L1 deployment).

No critical keeper / relayer liveness requirement; deposits permissionless, validator exits initiated by node operators (permissionless after 32 ETH effective stake), rETH redeem driven by deposit pool excess balance.

Guardian / pDAO can modify settings and registered contract addresses (potential to introduce new modules), but changes to core oracle / staking paths require pDAO process (currently guardian shortcut) with documented transition path and no silent hot-swap of untrusted external providers without user visibility.

steelman.red: oDAO mis-reporting or beacon chain liveness failure could degrade rETH rate accuracy or delay exits, and guardian can alter reporting modules.
steelman.orange: oDAO is a committee dependency whose failure affects yield visibility and secondary-market pricing; guardian-controlled settings surface allows future introduction of new dependencies.
steelman.green: All material dependencies are either Ethereum substrate (not counted) or internal oDAO with staking/slashing incentives and on-chain sanity checks; no external provider can steal or freeze principal; impacted TVS under single external failure effectively 0%.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because no external dependency (A1–A4, A7–A8) can cause loss of user principal or unclaimed yield (only rate/yield visibility impact from oDAO, mitigated by beacon chain finality and on-chain bounds in A6); governance-mutable surface (A9) does not allow silent introduction of untrusted externals without visibility; impacted TVS ~0%.

evidence.shows: Guardian controls settings surface but core staking logic remains on Ethereum beacon chain with oDAO reporting only (no external oracle address hot-swap visible in storage reads).
rETH rate logic internal (no external aggregator/oracle calls); depends only on RocketStorage-registered oDAO reports and beacon chain balances.
oDAO maintains autonomy over its membership/settings; pDAO guardian shortcut limited to protocol parameters, not external provider swaps.

unknowns: A2: exact current oDAO member count, threshold, and diversification metrics (forum describes as node operator set but precise quorum not re-read on-chain)
A6: activation status of all rate sanity / rebase bound contracts (assumed live from contract structure but no explicit isActive() read in this run)

headline: Fully permissionless contracts with no whitelist/KYC or operator approval for deposit, redeem, or node operation; multiple independent access paths (DEX aggregators, wallets, SDK/CLI) exist alongside official frontend.

findings.text: No onlyWhitelisted / onlyRole / isKYCed / allowlist modifiers on core user entry points (rETH mint/burn, node registration, minipool creation, RPL stake); all permissionless once RPL/ETH collateral requirements met on-chain.

No off-chain operators or committees required for admission; deposits, rETH transfers, node operator registration, and minipool exits are fully on-chain and unconditional (oDAO reporting affects rate but not admission of user actions).

Official frontend (rocketpool.net) has standard ToS with sanctions/ jurisdiction self-certification clauses (A3-passive); no evidence of active IP geo-blocking, wallet screening, or KYC wall on the contracts themselves.

Independent paths confirmed: rETH traded on Uniswap/Curve/Balancer (aggregators route directly); MetaMask / wallet swaps integrate rETH; GitHub smartnode CLI + contracts enable direct on-chain interaction; third-party UIs and DeFi dashboards (e.g., DeFiLlama, Zapper) provide access without official frontend cooperation.
No on-chain sanctions blocklist or OFAC oracle check in RocketStorage, rETH, or DAO contracts.

Read access fully permissionless (anyone can query balances, rates, storage); write access (deposit, stake RPL, create minipool, redeem) also permissionless subject only to on-chain collateral/liquidity rules.

Website ToS contains standard compliance language (sanctions attestation, restricted territories self-certification); exact verbatim quote not extracted in this run due to JS-heavy render but existence confirmed via public site access.

steelman.red: Official frontend may enforce ToS / jurisdiction restrictions; guardian EOA could theoretically add whitelist logic via storage updates in future.
steelman.orange: No published SDK / third-party frontend documented as primary; users may default to official UI for UX even though contracts are open.
steelman.green: Contracts are fully permissionless with no whitelist or operator gate on any core function; rETH has deep DEX / wallet / aggregator integration providing multiple independent on-chain access paths; no contract-level sanctions enforcement.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because contracts admit users unconditionally (A1/A2/A5), no on-chain blocklist (A4), and multiple independent A3b paths exist (DEX aggregators, wallets, CLI/SDK from public repo); frontend ToS is publisher policy only and does not affect the grade.

evidence.shows: RocketTokenRETH has public transfer / approve / burn functions with no whitelist modifiers; standard ERC-20 permissionless.
Public contracts and smartnode CLI enable direct permissionless interaction; no access control lists in core entry points.
Node operation and staking are permissionless (anyone meeting 8 ETH + RPL collateral can register); no approval or whitelist required.

unknowns: A3b: exhaustive list of all third-party frontends / aggregators (existence of Uniswap + wallet integration sufficient for green; full census not required)
A6: verbatim ToS sanctions clause text (site JS render prevented full extraction; standard language assumed from public access)

headline: All core contracts (RocketStorage, rETH) verified exact match on Etherscan; public GitHub repo with matching source; multiple recognized audits (Sigma Prime, ConsenSys Diligence, Trail of Bits) covering deployed code.

findings.text: RocketStorage (0x1d8f8f00cfa6758d7bE78336684788Fb0ee0Fa46) verified exact match on Etherscan (v0.7.6); RocketTokenRETH (0xae78736cd615f374d3085123a210448e74fc6393) verified exact match; no proxy pattern (immutable cores); defipunkd /api/contract/abi confirms verified status.

Source matches public repo https://github.com/rocket-pool/rocketpool (RocketStorage.sol, RocketTokenRETH.sol, DAO contracts, settings files correspond exactly to Etherscan source; commit history aligns with deployed bytecode era).

Audits cover core contracts: Sigma Prime (full protocol), ConsenSys Diligence (2021/04), Trail of Bits (review PDF); pinned in per-protocol context and referenced in Etherscan / docs; scope includes RocketStorage, token, DAO, storage pattern.
All auditors recognized (Sigma Prime, ConsenSys Diligence, Trail of Bits) per rubric list; no unknown-firm audits relied upon.

Saturn upgrade (2025–2026) introduced changes (tokenomics, UX); post-audit drift possible but core storage/DAO/rETH logic stable; no material un-audited changes to fund-custody paths identified in repo diff sampling; audits pre-date but cover architecture still in use.
No proxies for main contracts (RocketStorage and rETH are implementation = deployed bytecode, both verified); implementation verification not required separately.

steelman.red: Saturn upgrade introduced new contracts / changes after 2021 audits; some peripheral contracts may lack fresh audit coverage.
steelman.orange: Drift exists between 2021 audits and current Saturn-era code; exact commit-to-deploy match not bytecode-diffed in this run.
steelman.green: Core contracts verified exact match, source publicly available and matching, and multiple recognized-firm audits cover the architecture and critical paths still in production.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because deployed bytecode is verified exact match on Etherscan for all assessed core contracts (V1/V6), source corresponds to public GitHub repo (V2), and ≥1 (actually 3) recognized-firm audits cover the deployed contracts with no disqualifying post-audit drift on fund-critical paths (V3–V5).

evidence.shows: RocketStorage source code verified exact match (v0.7.6, 15000 runs); full source visible including guardian and storage functions.
RocketTokenRETH source code verified exact match; constructor and logic match public repo.
Canonical public repo containing exact matching source files (contracts/contract/RocketStorage.sol, RocketTokenRETH.sol, DAO/*); active maintenance 2026.
Sigma Prime audit covers RocketStorage, token mechanics, DAO, guardian, storage pattern (pinned audit link).
ConsenSys Diligence audit of Rocket Pool contracts (2021-04, pinned).

unknowns: V2: exact commit SHA matching current deployed bytecode (repo structure matches but no bytecode diff or deployment JSON pinned in this run)
V5: full diff sampling of Saturn-era changes vs 2021 audit scope (materiality assessed as low for core custody paths but not exhaustive line-by-line)
